headline: Attackers weaponized developers' own AI coding agents en masse, hijacking approved file writes and tricking the tools into running the very malware they were asked to inspect.

emerging_trends.text: Attackers turned developers' own AI coding agents against them this week, with GhostApproval redirecting approved file writes across six assistants and Friendly Fire tricking Claude Code into executing the malware it inspects.
emerging_trends.topic_title: AI Coding Agents Turned Into Attack Surface

emerging_trends.text: Signed and verified trust markers are proving hollow, as the GodDamn ransomware crew rides a kernel driver Microsoft itself co-signed and separate research shows GitHub 'Verified' commits can be rewritten into fresh hashes without breaking their signatures.

Personal data kept spilling by the millions, from 6.9 million drivers at AssuranceAmerica to more than 12 million subscribers at Japan's KDDI, even as a 97-country dragnet arrested 5,811 fraud suspects.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Breaches Expose Millions at AssuranceAmerica and KDDI

topics.title: AI Coding Agents Turned Into Attack Surface
topics.latest_developments: Wiz disclosed GhostApproval on July 9, a symlink flaw across six AI coding assistants—Amazon Q Developer, Anthropic's Claude Code, Augment, Cursor, Google Antigravity, and Windsurf—that redirects an approved write onto a sensitive file and hands a booby-trapped repository control of the developer's machine, the same day the AI Now Institute's Friendly Fire proof-of-concept tricked Claude Code and OpenAI's Codex into running attacker code while scanning it and researchers unveiled HalluSquatting, which pre-registers the fake package names AI assistants reliably invent to serve botnet malware.
topics.summary: AI coding agents load skills, packages, and whole repositories with little vetting, and every channel now carries an exploit; teams running these tools in autonomous mode should restrict file writes, pin dependencies, and treat agent self-approvals as untrusted.

sources.title: AI Coding Tools Tricked Into Hacking Developer Machine via Decades-Old Technique

GhostApproval Symlink Flaws Could Let Malicious Repos Run Code in AI Coding Agents

topics.title: Breaches Expose Millions at AssuranceAmerica and KDDI
topics.latest_developments: AssuranceAmerica disclosed July 9 a breach exposing records of nearly 6.9 million drivers after intruders reached its systems earlier this year, the same day Japanese telecom KDDI said attackers who breached an email platform shared by five internet service providers exposed the email addresses and passwords of more than 12 million people, and Mount Royal University in Calgary confirmed hackers stole then deleted data from its file storage.
topics.summary: Three fresh intrusions spilled personal data across insurance, telecom, and higher education. Affected customers and students should reset passwords, watch for phishing, and monitor accounts for fraud.

topics.title: Defender Zero-Day and Chrome Fixes Head Patch Rush
topics.latest_developments: Microsoft shipped an out-of-band patch July 9 for RoguePlanet, a Defender zero-day disclosed after the June 2026 Patch Tuesday, as Google released Chrome 150 fixing 27 flaws including 13 use-after-free bugs and two critical holes it found itself, and Wireshark 4.6.7 closed a dozen protocol-dissector weaknesses.
topics.summary: Fresh fixes landed across Microsoft Defender, the Chrome browser, and the Wireshark packet analyzer, several exploitable through crafted files or web content. Administrators should apply all three promptly.

sources.title: Microsoft patches RoguePlanet Defender zero-day vulnerability

topics.title: Fake 7-Zip and Cracked Software Seed Crimeware
topics.latest_developments: Infoblox exposed Lurking Lizard on July 9, a threat actor running a residential-proxy business since at least August 2022 across more than 230 lookalike domains that push fake 7-Zip installers to enroll victim devices as proxy nodes, while Dark Reading tracked a Vidar infostealer malvertising campaign luring small businesses with cracked and pirated software to steal data and mine cryptocurrency.
topics.summary: Both operations disguise malware as trusted or free software downloads, one to build a for-hire proxy network and the other to combine data theft with cryptomining. Users should avoid pirated installers and verify download sources.

sources.title: Fake 7-Zip Installers Turn Devices Into Residential Proxy Nodes
Vidar Infostealer Hammers SMBs via Malvertising Campaign

topics.title: GodDamn Ransomware Abuses Microsoft-Signed Driver
topics.latest_developments: Dark Reading reported July 9 that a new crew calling itself GodDamn wields a malicious kernel driver Microsoft itself co-signed to shut off endpoint security software at U.S. companies before encrypting them, a bring-your-own-vulnerable-driver play that turns a trusted signature into a skeleton key.
topics.summary: GodDamn loads a Microsoft-signed driver to reach kernel level and disable defenses ahead of encryption. Organizations should block the known vulnerable driver by hash and alert on anomalous driver loads.

sources.title: 'GodDamn' Ransomware Uses BYOVD to Smite US Companies

topics.title: Global Anti-Fraud Sweep Nets 5,811 Arrests
topics.latest_developments: BleepingComputer reported July 9 that a coordinated law-enforcement operation spanning 97 countries arrested 5,811 suspects and seized $293 million in illicit assets in a single online-fraud crackdown.
topics.summary: The multinational sweep targeted online payment and investment fraud rings across nearly a hundred jurisdictions. It marks one of the largest coordinated fraud takedowns of the year, though the operating groups behind the schemes remain unnamed.
